title: feat(scripts): gate documented SchemaExample ids against the catalog registry
body:
Fixes objectui#8623

## What this adds

`check:doc-example-ids` — a static check that every `SchemaExample` reference in
`content/docs/**` names an id the schema catalog registry actually carries, plus its
test and its own workflow.

`SchemaExample` resolves its `id` prop through `getExample`, and that lookup **throws**
on an unknown id rather than degrading. Per the triage ruling that behaviour is
**unchanged here** — no fallback in `getExample`, and no registry entry added so a
reference resolves. What was missing is that nothing asked the question *before* render,
so a mistyped or stale id passed every check in the repository and crashed the page it
was on.

## The population — re-measured on this branch point, not inherited

`origin/main` had moved from the sha named in the dispatch (`e8b7b078` -> `9b83f479`), so
the reading was retaken:

| reading | count |
|:--|--:|
| pages walked under `content/docs/**` (`.mdx` + `.md`) | 184 |
| `SchemaExample` references found | 416 (415 distinct) |
| ids in the catalog registry | 432 |
| references that resolve | 414 |
| references exempted as illustrative | 2 |
| **real references that do not resolve** | **0** |

**Control:** the intersection is non-empty (414 of 416), so the misses are a reading and
not a broken matcher. The registry itself is read twice from the generated index — the
`REGISTRY` object's own keys, which is what `getExample` indexes, and the schema import
specifiers above them — and the two must agree exactly or the gate reports *could not
run*.

Both exemptions are the syntax placeholders in the schema-catalog authoring guide, exactly
as the dispatch measured: the angle-bracket template in the snippet teaching the tag, and
the ellipsis in the prose sentence describing it. **There is not one broken real id in the
docs today.**

## The exemption is a shape rule, not a list of two literals

A value carrying angle-bracket metasyntax, or an elision (Unicode or ASCII), cannot be a
filename-derived id — so it is illustrative. That rule is argued in the script's header
and it is never silent: every run prints each exemption with its page, its value and the
marker that matched. Two things it deliberately does **not** do:

- It does not exempt a value that is merely *wrong*. Bad case, wrong segment count, a
  typo — all still judged. A pinned test fixtures a well-formed typo and requires it red.
- It does not trust its own premise. `assertMarkersAreImpossible` re-derives from the live
  registry on every run that no real id carries a marker, and exits *could not run* if that
  ever stops holding, rather than letting the exemption swallow a real reference.

## Green on landing proves nothing — so here is the gate going red

**Firing control, on the real tree.** One real id in a layout docs page was mutated to a
typo, the gate was run, and the page was restored. Restoration is proved by hash rather
than by an exit code — pre-mutation blob `36867f58`, post-mutation `f216a5ca`,
post-restore `36867f58`, and `git diff HEAD` empty:

```
=== GATE EXIT ON MUTATED TREE = 1
Doc example ids — walked 184 page(s) under content/docs, found 416 SchemaExample reference(s) (415 distinct), against 432 catalog id(s).

Exempted 2 illustrative reference(s) — metasyntax, never an id:
  content/docs/guide/schema-catalog.mdx (line 15)  id="…"  — elision
  content/docs/guide/schema-catalog.mdx (line 44)  id="[angle-bracket template]"  — angle-bracket metavariable

⛔ 1 reference(s) name an id the catalog registry does not carry:
  content/docs/components/layout/card.mdx (line 8)  id="components-layout-card/basic-crad"

Each one is a throw at page render in the published docs, not a blank tile. Fix the id, or add the schema and regenerate the catalog index. ⛔ Do not make getExample fall back — a silently wrong example teaches the wrong thing.
```

(The two exempted values are shown with the angle-bracket one written out in words; the
run prints the literal.)

**Firing control, in the test.** `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-example-ids.test.ts` spawns
the **real script as a process** over throwaway trees — not a unit test of a helper —
and asserts exit `1` for an unknown id, exit `1` for a tag with no id at all, and exit `0`
once the same fixture's id is corrected, so the red was the id and not the fixture.

**Non-empty-population controls.** A walk that reads zero pages, a matcher that finds zero
references, and a registry that reads as zero ids each exit `2` (*could not run*), because
all three otherwise produce the same clean verdict as a clean tree. Each has its own pin.

**Verdict on the restored tree**, at final HEAD `61dd16b56`:

```
Doc example ids — walked 184 page(s) under content/docs, found 416 SchemaExample reference(s) (415 distinct), against 432 catalog id(s).

Exempted 2 illustrative reference(s) — metasyntax, never an id:
  content/docs/guide/schema-catalog.mdx (line 15)  id="…"  — elision
  content/docs/guide/schema-catalog.mdx (line 44)  id="[angle-bracket template]"  — angle-bracket metavariable

✅ 414 real reference(s) all resolve in the catalog registry.
```

## Why a fourth `check-doc-*` script and not a leg on one of the three

Each neighbour's header was read before this one was named, and none can be extended
without blurring a question it declares it answers alone:

- the doc-example **types** checker compiles fenced ts/tsx inside JSDoc `@example` comments
  on exported declarations under `packages/*/src/**`, against the built `.d.ts` — a
  different population, a different instrument, a different universe;
- the doc-example **shared-reader** checker asks whether a doc comment hand-spells a ladder
  a published shared reader owns, and its header rules `content/docs/**` out explicitly;
- the doc **component-types** checker is closest in shape — it walks these same pages and
  derives its universe from source every run, which is why this script borrows both habits
  — but its subject is a `type` string literal inside a fenced code block judged against the
  component registry, and its header states it answers one question only. An example id is a
  JSX attribute in the page's prose judged against the example catalog; folding two
  vocabularies into one gate makes its verdict line ambiguous for no shared work.

The script name and the `check:doc-example-ids` alias collide with none of the three, and a
pin asserts all four still point at their own files.

## Wiring: its own workflow, not a `lint.yml` leg

The dispatch asked for a workflow leg. It got its own workflow, for the reason the
doc-component-types workflow header records for the neighbouring gate over these same pages:
the change that introduces this defect is **docs-only**, and that is precisely the shape
`ci.yml` and `lint.yml` short-circuit — `ci.yml`'s `type-check` job decides with a `git diff`
that excludes `content/**`. Wired into `lint.yml`, this gate would be blind to every change
that can introduce the defect. It needs no install and no build, so it can afford to run
unfiltered. This also leaves the `lint.yml` seam with objectui#8554 untouched entirely; the
only shared file is the `package.json` scripts block, one added line.

## Two files beyond the declared face, both forced by existing pins

Running the whole `scripts/__tests__` suite turned two pins red on the new workflow, and
both are wiring the repository already requires:

- the CI/CD pipeline guide needs a section naming the workflow file plus an inventory row —
  a workflow nobody documented is a check contributors get blocked by without knowing it
  exists;
- the Dependabot merge gate must classify every check a pull request produces exactly once.
  The new check subscribes `pull_request` with no trigger-level path filter, so it goes in
  the required set beside the three neighbouring doc gates.

⚠️ The docs page edited is the **CI guide**, not a page this gate reads for ids, and it was
not edited to make any check pass — it was edited because an existing pin requires it. No
`content/docs` page's `SchemaExample` id was touched.

## Verification

Run under the shared verification lock where it holds cores; gate scripts read the checkout
only.

| what | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__` | 138 files passed, 2 skipped; **4026 tests passed** (26 of them this gate's) |
| the new gate on the real tree | exit 0, output above |
| the new gate on a mutated real tree | exit 1, output above |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.scripts.json` | exit 0 — and `--listFiles` confirms **both** new files are in that program, so it is a measurement rather than an exclusion |
| `eslint .` repo-wide, `--format json` | 4743 files linted; both new files 0 errors / 0 warnings. The 79 files with pre-existing errors are untouched by this branch, and the config enables no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict |
| changeset presence / no-major / fixed-group | exit 0 each; the presence gate's own verdict line: no released package's source or published contract changed, and a changeset is declared anyway |
| control bytes, action-ref convention, doc links, doc component types, doc fence languages, shell-escape residue, new cross-file line citations | exit 0 each |
| governed-surface guard `--test` over this diff | NOT GOVERNED — ordinary merge-queue route |

`check-doc-snippet-types` is not owed: the docs edit adds **zero** fenced blocks (`git diff`
`^+` fence count is 0), so no snippet population moved. Everything else is CI's.

## Boundaries honoured

- `getExample`'s throwing behaviour is untouched; no fallback, no registry entry added to
  make a reference resolve.
- The population stops at `content/docs/**`. `examples/`, the READMEs, the smoke test, the
  script test, the extractor CLI, the Python regenerator and the site's own components are
  all out, and the script's header says why.
- No test skipped, disabled or quarantined. `content/docs/releases/` untouched.
- `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` untouched (objectui#8554's file).

## ⚠️ One dispatch premise my own measurement falsified

**Premise 2 is false as stated.** It said the reference shape outside `content/docs` "still
lives in exactly the seven files the card listed". Measured tree-wide on this branch point it
lives in **nine**: the seven, plus the site's `SchemaExample` component and its
`SchemaCatalogIndex` sibling. The card's original grep was scoped to `scripts/ examples/
packages/`, which never contained `apps/`, so the seven-file reading was correct for that
scope and the dispatch generalised it one step too far. **Control:** the same command shape
over the same population returns 179 files for a term known to be everywhere, so the reader
was firing. This changes nothing about the ruling — both extra files are the machinery that
*consumes* ids rather than pages that reference them, and both are outside the population
triage scoped — but the dispatch's count is wrong and is recorded as wrong here.

Premises 1, 3 and 4 all held. The dispatch's population table (415 distinct / 432 registry /
413 resolving / 2 missing, both placeholders in the authoring guide) reproduced exactly on
the newer tip.
